notes.summary: Static GK gives 3 to 5 questions per paper: sports (terms, trophies, venues, winners), awards, books and authors, important days, and organisations with their headquarters. These are pure memory facts, so revise them as short lists every week. Results of recent events (who won in a given year) change, so pair this page with a monthly current affairs source.

concepts.title: Major events and India's champions
concepts.body:
• Olympics: modern Games began in Athens, 1896 (Pierre de Coubertin). IOC HQ: Lausanne. Recent and next: Tokyo 2020 (held 2021), Paris 2024, Los Angeles 2028, Brisbane 2032.
  • Asian Games: first in New Delhi, 1951. 2022 Games held at Hangzhou in 2023; 2026 at Aichi-Nagoya (Japan).
  • Commonwealth Games: first at Hamilton, Canada, 1930. 2022 Birmingham; 2026 Glasgow.
  • National Games: 36th Gujarat (2022), 37th Goa (2023), 38th Uttarakhand (2025).
India's Olympic landmarksFact
Hockey8 gold medals (1928 to 1980)
K.D. JadhavFirst individual medal, wrestling bronze, Helsinki 1952
Karnam MalleswariFirst Indian woman to win an Olympic medal, weightlifting bronze, Sydney 2000
Abhinav BindraFirst individual gold, shooting, Beijing 2008
Neeraj ChopraJavelin gold, Tokyo 2020; silver, Paris 2024
Manu BhakerTwo bronze medals at Paris 2024 (shooting)

Cricket: India won the ODI World Cup in 1983 (Kapil Dev) and 2011 (M.S. Dhoni); the T20 World Cup in 2007 and 2024; the Champions Trophy in 2002 (shared), 2013 and 2025. India's women won the ODI World Cup in 2025. Chess: D. Gukesh became the youngest world champion in December 2024.

concepts.title: National awards
concepts.body:
• Bharat Ratna (1954): highest civilian award. First (1954): C. Rajagopalachari, S. Radhakrishnan, C.V. Raman. First posthumous: Lal Bahadur Shastri (1966). First woman: Indira Gandhi (1971). Non-Indians: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (1987), Nelson Mandela (1990). Youngest: Sachin Tendulkar (2014). Usually at most 3 a year; 5 were named in 2024.
  • Padma awards (1954): Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, Padma Shri; announced on Republic Day eve.
  • Gallantry: wartime Param Vir Chakra (first: Major Somnath Sharma, 1947), Maha Vir Chakra, Vir Chakra. Peacetime Ashoka Chakra, Kirti Chakra, Shaurya Chakra.

concepts.title: International awards
concepts.body:
• Nobel Prize (from 1901; Alfred Nobel). Peace prize given in Oslo, others in Stockholm. Economics added in 1969.
  • Ramon Magsaysay Award ('Asia's Nobel', Philippines, 1957); first Indian winner Vinoba Bhave (1958).
  • Pulitzer Prize: journalism, books, music (USA, Columbia University).
  • Booker Prize: English fiction. Indian-origin winners: Salman Rushdie (Midnight's Children, 1981), Arundhati Roy (The God of Small Things, 1997), Kiran Desai (The Inheritance of Loss, 2006), Aravind Adiga (The White Tiger, 2008).
  • International Booker (translated fiction): Geetanjali Shree, Tomb of Sand (2022, Hindi); Banu Mushtaq, Heart Lamp (2025, Kannada).
  • Abel Prize and Fields Medal: mathematics (Fields for those under 40). Karen Uhlenbeck was the first woman to win the Abel Prize (2019). Turing Award: computing.
  • Oscars: Bhanu Athaiya was the first Indian winner (costume design, Gandhi, 1983 ceremony); Satyajit Ray got an honorary Oscar (1992); A.R. Rahman won two for Slumdog Millionaire (2009); Period. End of Sentence. won best documentary short (2019); 'Naatu Naatu' (RRR) won best original song and The Elephant Whisperers won best documentary short (2023).

varieties.name: Sports rules and terms
varieties.how: Learn players per side and a few terms for each sport. If a term fits two sports, look for the one only one sport uses (bully: hockey; chukker: polo; birdie: golf and badminton).

example.q: How many players does each volleyball team have on court?

varieties.name: Trophies, tournaments and stadiums
varieties.how: Learn trophies by sport, and men's versus women's pairs (Thomas and Uber, Swaythling and Corbillon). Learn stadiums with their city.

example.q: The Durand Cup is associated with which sport?
steps: Durand Cup started in 1888 at Shimla.
It is the oldest football tournament in Asia.

varieties.name: Sports events and champions
varieties.how: Learn host cities for the last and next Games and India's landmark medals. For yearly winners, use a current affairs source.

example.q: Who won India's first individual Olympic gold medal?
steps: K.D. Jadhav won bronze in 1952, not gold.
Abhinav Bindra won gold in 10 m air rifle at Beijing 2008.

varieties.name: Sports awards
varieties.how: Learn what each award is for (athlete, coach, university, organisation) and the rename of Khel Ratna in 2021.

example.q: The Dronacharya Award is given to:
steps: Dronacharya was the teacher of the Pandavas.
So the award honours sports coaches.

varieties.name: Awards and honours
varieties.how: Link each award to its field and its first winner. For the Nobel and Booker, learn the Indian winners with years.

example.q: Who was the first recipient of the Dadasaheb Phalke Award?
steps: The award began in 1969 for lifetime work in cinema.
Its first winner was actress Devika Rani.

varieties.name: Books and authors
varieties.how: Group books by era and by author. Watch for authors with many books (Nehru, Gandhi, Premchand, Kalam) and similar titles (A Passage to India vs A Passage to England).

steps: It is a memoir of the freedom struggle and partition talks.
The author is Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, not Nehru.

varieties.name: Important days and dates
varieties.how: Learn days month by month with the reason or person behind each. Birthdays give many Indian days.

example.q: National Science Day on 28 February marks:
steps: C.V. Raman announced his discovery on 28 February 1928.
So the day marks the discovery of the Raman effect.
example.answer: The discovery of the Raman effect

varieties.name: Organisations and headquarters
varieties.how: Group headquarters by city (Geneva, Vienna, Rome, Paris, New York). For Indian bodies, learn founder and year.

example.q: Which pair of bodies both have headquarters in Vienna?
steps: Vienna hosts IAEA, UNIDO and OPEC.
So IAEA and OPEC are the pair.

varieties.name: National symbols and Indian firsts
varieties.how: Learn each symbol with its adoption date, and each 'first' with the office or feat.

example.q: Who was the first woman Chief Minister in India?
steps: She became Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh in 1963.

tips: Geneva is for health, work and trade (WHO, ILO, WTO); Rome is for food (FAO, IFAD, WFP); Paris for culture (UNESCO); Nairobi for environment (UNEP).
Badminton and table tennis cups come in men-women pairs: Thomas-Uber, Swaythling-Corbillon.
Grand Slam surfaces in calendar order: hard (Australia), clay (France), grass (Wimbledon), hard (US).
Birthday days: Youth Day (Vivekananda), Teachers' Day (Radhakrishnan), Engineers' Day (Visvesvaraya), Sports Day (Dhyan Chand), Maths Day (Ramanujan).
First Bharat Ratnas (1954): 'RRR' gives Rajagopalachari, Radhakrishnan, Raman.
Golf scores: birdie 1 under, eagle 2 under, bogey 1 over.
traps: India Wins Freedom is by Maulana Azad, not Nehru (Nehru wrote Discovery of India).
A Passage to India is by E.M. Forster; A Passage to England is by Nirad C. Chaudhuri.
Davis Cup is tennis (men's teams); Thomas Cup is badminton.
Bharat Ratna 1954 did not go to Nehru; he received it in 1955.
The UN HQ is New York, but the International Court of Justice sits in The Hague.

questions.q: How many players are there on each side in a volleyball match?
questions.solution:
Volleyball has 6 players per side on court. Basketball has 5 and kabaddi has 7.
Memory hook: Volleyball court has 2 rows of 3 = 6.

questions.q: National Sports Day in India is celebrated on the birthday of:
questions.solution:
National Sports Day is on 29 August, the birthday of hockey wizard Major Dhyan Chand.
Memory hook: The Khel Ratna also carries his name — Dhyan Chand owns Indian sports honours.

Rabindranath Tagore wrote Gitanjali; its English version won him the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913.
Memory hook: Gitanjali = 'song offerings' by Gurudev Tagore.

questions.q: The Durand Cup is associated with which sport?
questions.solution:
The Durand Cup is a football tournament, one of the oldest in the world and the oldest in Asia (first held in 1888).
Memory hook: Durand and Santosh — India's two classic football cups.

questions.q: Who was the first recipient of the Dadasaheb Phalke Award?
questions.solution:
Devika Rani received the first Dadasaheb Phalke Award in 1969. She is called the 'First Lady of Indian Cinema'.
Memory hook: First award, First Lady of Indian Cinema.

questions.q: National Science Day is celebrated on 28 February to mark:
questions.solution:
C.V. Raman announced the Raman Effect on 28 February 1928. His birthday is 7 November.
Memory hook: Science Day celebrates the discovery, not the man's birthday.

questions.q: Which of the following was NOT among the first recipients of the Bharat Ratna in 1954?
questions.solution:
The first Bharat Ratna awards (1954) went to C. Rajagopalachari, Dr. S. Radhakrishnan and Dr. C.V. Raman. Nehru received it in 1955.
Memory hook: 'R-R-R': Rajagopalachari, Radhakrishnan, Raman.

options: Wings of Fire — A.P.J. Abdul Kalam
questions.solution:
'India Wins Freedom' is the autobiography of Maulana Abul Kalam Azad. Nehru wrote 'The Discovery of India'.
Memory hook: Azad = freedom; 'India Wins Freedom' belongs to Azad.
